content.title: THE MINERAL THAT CONTROLS YOUR {{THYROID}} AND NOBODY TALKS ABOUT IT
facts: **Iodine** – your thyroid literally cannot make its hormones without it, and those hormones run your metabolism, energy, and body temperature.
**Cod** – a 3oz serving covers most of your daily iodine needs in one simple meal.
**Seaweed Snacks** – even a small dried sheet packs a surprising amount of iodine, way more than most land foods.
**Eggs** – 2 eggs/day gives you a steady, easy iodine boost most people overlook.
**Baked Potato (with skin)** – an underrated source, especially if you rarely eat seafood.
**Dairy Milk** – 1 cup/day contributes meaningfully, thanks to iodine-based sanitizers used in dairy farming.
**Prunes** – 5 prunes/day is a quiet, fruity way to sneak in extra iodine.
**Follow along** – for more daily health tips like this.
content.caption:
Let's talk about iodine, because almost nobody brings it up until something feels off. Cod is one of the easiest wins here — your thyroid uses iodine from foods like this to build T3 and T4, the hormones that basically set the pace for your whole metabolism, so even a mild shortfall can leave you feeling sluggish. Seaweed snacks are a sneaky powerhouse too, since ocean plants pull iodine straight from seawater, making them one of the most concentrated natural sources around. And prunes might be the most underrated one on this list — they're not just a fiber food, they quietly add iodine to your day without you even noticing. Everyone's needs are a little different, so listen to your body and check with a doctor if something feels persistently off.
